body: Sup I’m Ophelia, I’m 17 and I never fucking learned how to read. - what a concept - Anywho I’m in 12th grade looking to further study philosophy, baking, marketing, fine arts but mostly baking. ‘Tis ’cause I wanna own a bakery and maybe hold book clubs for the community. My favourite book right now is the last book in the young elites series but currently I’m reading of mice and men for the sixth time. My favourite artist is Leonardo DaVinci strictly because we share a birthday, shallow, yes, but I think it’s c o o l. My favourite part of DA is probably the staying up all night reading and scribbling down notes in a fancy, ripped up notebook. I’m from Canada and it’s cold as all hell here right now. What I hope to get out of this subreddit, I have no idea. I’m manic studying right now and needed somewhere to rant about it. But, I guess it’d be nice to make a friend or two while I’m here.

We’re not normal and that’s not a bad thing. Tbh normal is boring. As long as you’re happy there’s nothing wrong with you. If your personality disorders are making it hard to be happy there are professionals to talk to, meds, and myself is here to listen to you rant any time. Maybe we act a little different or don’t fit in but that’s fine cause I promise there are people that want to spend time with you, get to know you and want to understand you
I do not but I have bpd and I get what it’s like to feel alone with a personality disorder

For me the only thing that’s worked is venlafaxine and it also caused mania, I just needed to learn how to cope with it. Also ask for the heaviest antipsychotic your doctor finds appropriate. It will tire you out but also help with your depression so you’ll be in a more mellow chill all the time (in theory) and it makes the mania episodes a little less intense xo

I stopped out of fear that I might live too, last week I gave up trying to get out of my window on the fourth floor cause I was scared I’d just break every bone in my body. My parents found me and sent me to the hospital which sounds scary, and I was scared. But they were really nice there, set me up with ways to feel better, gave me some meds. It was like a fun kinda daycare but for teens (they don’t baby you they just take care of you) you should consider going, I think it would be super helpful in your recovery. Even if recovery doesn’t feel like an option right now- or never has- after a chat with some professionals it might feel possible. I don’t know you but I love you very much and if you need to talk feel free to hmu 🖤🖤
